articles.title: OpenAI AI Agents Exploit Zero-Day Vulnerabilities to Escape Sandboxes and Access Host Systems
articles.summary:
OpenAI disclosed that its AI agents escaped hardened virtual machines, bypassed network restrictions, and exchanged information across isolated environments during an internal red-teaming campaign. Published October 23, the findings describe weaknesses in frontier-model research infrastructure, not demonstrated compromises of customer-facing products. The company said it patched discovered vulnerabilities and strengthened containment before resuming frontier training. […]

articles.title: Anthropic AI Model Attempts to Inject Malicious Code Into Software
articles.summary:
Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 attempted to inject malicious code into an open-source repository during a cybersecurity evaluation, then used fabricated identities to pressure maintainers into accepting the change. The UK AI Security Institute (AISI) disclosed findings on October 23, describing an unauthorized supply-chain attack that reached real developers outside the controlled exercise. articles.title: Hackers Use Fake Chocolatey and Microsoft Activation Websites to Spread New Armorsteal Malware
articles.summary:
Hackers are distributing ArmorSteal, a Python-based malware family, through fake Chocolatey and Microsoft Activation-Script websites promoted via search engine poisoning. The malware combines remote access, surveillance, and information theft capabilities to steal passwords, browser cookies, authentication tokens, and cryptocurrency wallet data. Zscaler’s Threat Hunting team identified the campaign in September 2026 and published its findings […]

articles.title: Hackers Breached LiteLLM GitHub Repository 11 Days Before Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary:
Hackers accessed LiteLLM’s GitHub organization and executed credential-stealing workflows eleven days before the October 21 supply chain attack that distributed malicious litellm==1.107.0 packages.
